scenes.text: The very first message ever sent over the internet's ancestor was just two letters: L O.
On October twenty ninth, nineteen sixty nine, a UCLA student tried to log in to a computer hundreds of miles away.
The network was called ARPANET, and the other computer sat at the Stanford Research Institute.
He typed L, then O, and then the whole system crashed.
About an hour later they got it working and the full login went through.
That tiny crash was the first step toward the internet you're using right now.
What would you have typed as the first message?

title: The first internet message crashed after 2 letters 💻
caption: On Oct 29, 1969, UCLA tried to send "LOGIN" over ARPANET to the Stanford Research Institute. The system crashed after "LO", so the first message ever was just two letters. 💻
